absent: Full struct layouts for wakeup_header, saved_context, desc_ptr, msr, alt_instr, its_array, insn, and module arch data including offsets and sizes.
Semantics of generic suspend helpers save_processor_state, restore_processor_state, save_registers, restore_registers, and graph tracing pause helpers.
Initial page table, real mode header, and per CPU data organization beyond observed field uses.
Complete alternative rewriting pipeline including relocation application and idle fill optimization internals.
Execmem allocation, strict permission restoration, and module text lifecycle beyond ITS page bookkeeping.
APIC callback registry behavior and multiprocessor wakeup sequencing beyond mailbox installation.
Video mode preservation, nonvolatile storage handling, blacklist, and ordering effects referenced by boot tokens.
Exact fault reporting, warning emission, and early patch publication mechanisms.

findings.text: The helper acpi_setup_mp_wakeup_mailbox records the firmware mailbox location and repoints secondary bringup toward acpi_wakeup_cpu. The recorded mapping is later readable through acpi_get_mp_wakeup_mailbox while the raw location is readable through acpi_get_mp_wakeup_mailbox_paddr.

The low real mode area exposes the firmware wakeup vector through acpi_get_wakeup_address. Sleep transitions are requested through x86_acpi_enter_sleep_state which forwards the requested state to the generic sleep helper and returns its status.

The routine x86_acpi_suspend_lowlevel is the central suspend orchestrator. It rejects mismatched wakeup headers with an error and otherwise captures control state, selects the appropriate resume vector for the active word size, and transfers to the low level sleep helper with tracing paused.

Resume is permitted only when header and magic markers agree with the values installed before sleep. Behavior flags record which extended processor features were successfully probed for restore, so the wake path restores only what was previously verified as writable.

The structure wakeup_header shared with firmware holds a signature plus video and behavior settings plus control register snapshots plus split halves for extended features plus real mode options plus magic plus resume addresses. The real mode options originate in acpi_realmode_flags and are copied before sleep.

Low level sleep entries named do_suspend_lowlevel preserve processor and register state across the firmware sleep request and provide an inline recovery path when sleep fails. Distinct 32 bit and 64 bit wake vectors named wakeup_pmode_return and wakeup_long64 reestablish segment state, validate magic, and transfer to the previously saved resume point.

Suspend to memory moves from running to state captured to sleep requested to either inline failure recovery or firmware vectored resume to state restored. The vectored path is selected by word size while the inline path returns directly to the caller for restoration.

On 64 bit multiprocessor resumes the incoming processor is given a dedicated temporary stack and a deterministic identity unless parallel bringup is active. The temporary stack lives in temp_stack and is sized to hold early resume usage before the true stack is restored.

The temporary resume stack holds 4096 bytes. The 32 bit magic is 0x12345678 while the 64 bit magic is 0x123456789abcdef0, and a mismatch on 64 bit loads 0xbad6d61676963 before halting. The low level sleep request uses state value 3.

Early boot option parsing through acpi_sleep_setup recognizes tokens for video handling, beep, nonvolatile storage policy, ordering, blacklist, and hibernation signature control. A separate init helper named init_s4_sigcheck establishes the default hibernation signature policy when left unspecified.
The control acpi_check_s4_hw_signature remains at a sentinel until init time. When still unset on a virtualized host the check is enabled by default to honor firmware expectations across resume.

Real mode option bit zero corresponds to s3_bios, bit one to s3_mode, and bit two to s3_beep. Additional boot tokens include s4_hwsig and s4_nohwsig for signature policy plus nonvs and nonvs_s3 for storage policy plus old_ordering and nobl for ordering and blacklist control. Tokens are separated by commas with surrounding blanks skipped.

A global flag named alternatives_patched records whether alternative rewriting has occurred. Boot time debug selection is offered through debug_alt which interprets an optional numeric argument into debug_alternative, defaulting to all categories when absent or unparsable. Diagnostic lines carry a fixed multiprocessor alternatives prefix.

The longest single patch spans 254 bytes. Debug selection uses all bits set for full tracing, with 0x01 for alternative and 0x02 for return and 0x04 for retpoline and 0x08 for endbranch and 0x10 for multiprocessor categories.

The descriptor patch_site captures a target named instr plus a metadata reference named alt plus a scratch area named buff sized by the patch limit plus a length named len. The scratch area accommodates the maximum patch span.

The tables x86nops and x86_nops provide packed idle fill with indexed entries by desired length. Coverage extends through eight bytes generally and through eleven bytes on 64 bit builds, with index zero meaning no fill.

Module scoped thunk handling is bracketed by its_init_mod and its_fini_mod with teardown through its_free_mod. Static thunks remain reachable through its_static_thunk which adjusts for paranoid guard layout when enabled.

Module thunk preparation serializes on the text mutex. The init path acquires the mutex and records the active module while clearing the page cursor. The fini path clears both and releases the mutex, warning when the finished module differs from the recorded one.

Thunk storage grows one page at a time with bookkeeping for later protection and release. Fresh pages are filled with trap bytes and allocation starts beyond an initial reserved area, skipping to the upper half of a cache line when the branch would otherwise land low. Final protection restores execute only permissions under strict configurations.

Cache lines span 64 bytes with bit 0x20 distinguishing the upper half. Fresh thunk pages reserve the first 32 bytes and place branches upstairs. Thunks occupy three or four bytes depending on register width, plus three more when paranoid guards are active, with static paranoid entries starting two bytes early.

Retpoline rewriting over a range is offered through apply_retpolines. Whether return thunks are desired generally or at a particular address is queryable through cpu_wants_rethunk and cpu_wants_rethunk_at.

Each recorded site is decoded and classified by opcode shape. Recognized direct branches to thunk areas are rewritten according to active mitigations, while unrecognized or paranoid guarded shapes are left untouched. Successful rewrites are optimized for idle fill and published early.

Conditional 32 bit branches are recognized by a two byte escape pattern and rewritten by inverting the condition around an indirect transfer. Indirect encodings account for extended registers with an extra prefix byte and forbid the stack register. Padding favors segment prefixes or trap bytes depending on branch kind and available slack.

Rip relative calls use opcode 0xff with modrm 0x15. Conditional short forms span 0x70 through 0x7f while 32 bit conditionals use escape 0x0f with second byte in 0x80 through 0x8f. Fence insertion uses 0x0f then 0xae then 0xe8, segment padding uses 0x2e, extended registers add prefix 0x41, and trap fill uses 0xcc. Paranoid guards prepend 0xd6 then 0x75 then 0xfd, with indirect jumps as 0xff and base 0xe0 plus register.

Mismatched resume magic diverts to a fault path on 32 bit and halts in place on 64 bit. Invalid patch shapes, illegal stack register use, and failed thunk allocation are reported while leaving original bytes untouched. The helper BUG_func always traps.
The helper text_poke_apply_relocation applies relocations to a scratch buffer and then optimizes idle fill. The helper BUG_func provides an unconditional trap for patch sites that must never execute.
Return thunk desire depends on a processor feature flag. When the active return thunk is not the Strauss variant the desire is unconditional, otherwise only lower half addresses request it.
